chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus ibn Abd al-Rahman, who said: Is'haq ibn 'Ammar narrated to me, saying:

I asked Abu Ibrahim (peace be upon him) about a man whom the women claimed, to the exclusion of the men, after their men had passed away and their lineage had become extinct. He became a man, they married him off, and admitted him into their homes. A house was in the possession of a man. The clan of the men and the women who had become extinct sent for him and adjured him by Allah not to give their right to one who was not from them. The man in whose possession the house was knew his story and that he was a claimant as I described to you, and the matter was confused for him; he did not know whether to hand it over to the man, or to the clan of the women, or the clan of the men.

He (peace be upon him) said to me: 'Hand it over to the one whom he knows that the right is for them, based on his own knowledge, meaning the clan of the women, because no inheritance was established for this claimant by the claim of the women for him.'
ai.seo_question: How is inheritance distributed when a man is claimed by both female and male clans after the male lineage has become extinct?
ai.summary: In this ruling from al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) resolves an inheritance dispute where a man is claimed by women after the male lineage has perished, prioritizing the 'knowledge' (ma'rifa) of the women who admitted him over the male clan's claim. This highlights the Shia jurisprudential principle that actual, verified knowledge of lineage supersedes presumptive claims, especially in the absence of male heirs. The decision underscores the importance of the claimant's established relationship and the women's active role in validating the heir's status.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from Muhammad Bin Isa, from Yunus Bin Abdul Rahman, from Is’haq Bin Ammar who said,

‘I asked Abu Ibrahim<sup>asws</sup> (7<sup>th</sup> Imam<sup>asws</sup>) about a man who claimed to the women besides the men, after the going away of their men and becoming extinct. And he became a man and they got him married and entered him into their chambers, and in the hands of a man was a house. So the relatives of the men and the women who had become extinct had asked him, and adjured him by Allah<sup>azwj</sup>, that he would not give their rights to the one who was not from them, and the man in whose hand was the house knew the story, and he had a claimant just as I have described to you<sup>asws</sup>, and the matter was confusing to him, and he does not know whether to hand it over to the man, or to the relatives of the women, or relatives of the men’.

He (the narrator) said, ‘So he<sup>asws</sup> said to me: ‘Hand it over to the one whom he recognises that the right is for them upon his understanding with which he understands, meaning the relatives of the women, because he does not recognise for this claimant (the man), any inheritance by the claiming of the women for him’.
en.sarwar: 1. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from Muhammad ibn ‘Isa from Yunus ibn ‘Abd al-Rahman who has narrated the following: “Ishaq ibn ‘Ammar narrated to me that

he once asked abu Ibrahim, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about the case of a man against whom a woman without a man had laid a claim when their men were no more. When he became a man, the women married him and allowed him to enter their homes. A man had a house in his possession. The relatives of men and women who were no more asked him on oath not to give their right to those who do not have any right. The man who had the house in his possession knew the story of the man that he is being claimed as I mentioned but he is confused and does not know to whom he must give it; must he give it to the man or to the relatives of the women or to the relatives of men?

He (the Imam) said, ‘He must give it to the one whom he knows is rightful to the best of his knowledge, that is, the relatives of the women because he does not know of any right for inheritance in favor of the man just because the women have claimed him. 5 ”
